scope: Organization relevance only; no candidate grades, new candidate endorsements or financial totals. FEC identity uses exact committee IDs; CAL-ACCESS has a separate namespace. Unknown relevance is not evidence of irrelevance.

aipac-politics.excerpt: United Democracy Project, the AIPAC-backed super PAC
aipac-politics.finding: AIPAC describes advocacy for the US-Israel relationship, its PAC supporting pro-Israel congressional candidates, and UDP as an AIPAC-backed super PAC.

jstreet-criteria.excerpt: Support for a strong US-Israel relationship and for US security assistance to Israel that adheres to US law.
jstreet-criteria.finding: Criteria also include Palestinian rights, a negotiated Palestinian state, opposition to occupation/annexation, and humanitarian assistance. These differ from AIPAC’s policy criteria.

jstreet-action.excerpt: J Street Action Fund Super PAC
jstreet-action.finding: The September 10, 2026 entry identifies J Street Action Fund as J Street’s super PAC; J Street describes its political work as pro-Israel, pro-peace and pro-democracy.

track-aipac.excerpt: Paid for by Citizens Against AIPAC Corruption
track-aipac.finding: Track AIPAC describes opposition to AIPAC/Israel-lobby influence and support for candidates refusing Israel-lobby support. The page identifies Citizens Against AIPAC Corruption as its sponsor.

cair-action.excerpt: including supporting the violence in Gaza and opposing a ceasefire
cair-action.finding: CAIR Action evaluates civil rights and foreign policy. Endorsed indicates strong alignment; Preferred can mean a better alternative without full alignment; opposition can reflect Gaza/ceasefire or Islamophobia concerns. No endorsement can reflect insufficient information.

vote-for-peace.finding: Vote for Peace evaluates democracy, human rights, war-lobby/AIPAC funding and electoral viability. It aggregates aligned organizations’ recommendations and says inclusion alone is not endorsement.

dmfi.excerpt: DMFI is the home for pro-Israel Democrats
dmfi.finding: The joint DMFI/DMFI PAC page describes support for a pro-Israel Democratic majority and a strong US-Israel alliance, explicitly noting the two are separate organizations.

bold-udp.finding: Recipient Schedule A and UDP Schedule B independently record a 2026 intercommittee contribution. No candidate earmarking is established.

edw-udp.finding: Recipient Schedule A and UDP Schedule B independently record a 2026 intercommittee contribution. No candidate earmarking is established.

314-action-udp.finding: Recipient Schedule A and UDP Schedule B both report a 2024 intercommittee contribution; this is historical funding, not proof of current receipts or candidate earmarking.

palmetto-action-udp.finding: UDP reports a positive, non-memo intercommittee contribution to this exact FEC recipient ID. This is not a candidate earmark. Recipient-side confirmation was not returned by the Schedule A query; retain donor attribution.
